posts.text: BotW wasn't my first Zelda game but it was the one that made me into a Zelda fan if that makes sense, so my preference wpuld also be for BotW stuff, well actually BotW / TotK stuff. If you enjoyed Breath of the Wild you're almost guaranteed to like Tears of the kingdom too! Though I have played games beyond those 2, starting with oracle of seasons (that I think I was was too young and unfamiliar with games to understand) and then Twilight Princess which was a good game and then after BotW made me a fan of a franchise I've played pretty much every title on the Switch which does not include Ocarina of Time so it's kind of a shame to me that that's the only game they've converted outside of half the Deku tree! However I am looking to change that then the remake comes round! I was initially thinking of waiting for Pokémon WiWa to get a switch 2 but with this game I might just get one sooner. Is it not? Okay maybe not 95% but especially considering Lego's almost exclusively made sets for a game that's a year older than I am I think they know that majority of fans are adults. Both sound good, I was definitely thinking of a map too but I think TotK (it's map being an expanded BotW map) offers more than the BotW one but you said you've not played TotK yet so you'll have to try it and see! Though after saying all that about the map I do think I'd prefer something minifig scaled like the boko camp. 4 in a 20 set shouldn't be seen as some unattainable dream but you're probably right nonetheless. I think a Zelda CMF would be a great way to get more characters, I'm not sure if I'd just want wild era stuff or Zelda wide. But you could easily have a red and blue boko in the set and then gold or silver in the CMF, with different horn options for BotW and TotK. Black boko on horse back could slip into a guardian set to complete the gang. Guardian battle makes a lot of sense and honestly Ultra build lends itself so well to the Lego style. I think any of the dragons would be a great choice. I remember the first time I saw Farosh in BotW I was just in awe. The light dragon is definitely the important one though so that'd be my pick. A master sword sheath would be very low down the list of minifig parts I'd like to see from Zelda too. These are all great. I can see a battle talus set with some bokos easily. Octanethermoplastic has a lot of great Zelda builds (thanks to @Lyichir for pointing me in their direction). Hmm, I do think that for a wild era town build lookout landing would make most sense, you could still do it roughly to scale without it being insanely huge and you could easily include representatives from the different tribes and even several important names characters. Lookout landing having a Skyveiwbtower, mini stable and shop all help too.Though I don't know what they'd do about the underground section if they skip it or do a Harry Potter bank style approach. Guardian attack would be a great set but yeah proper set waves could have so much material and link has so many outfits he could be repeated across set without it being as repetitive as The Mandalorian, Harry Potter, Spider-man or Darth Vader.

posts.title: Marvel Superheroes 2026 - Rumors & Discussion
posts.text: Wanda and Pietro joined Hydra due to a feeling of powerlessness wanting personal revenge directed at Stark solely because his name was on the missile. I disagree with the other commentor remarking they are chaotic evil at any stage in Phase 1-3, they are misguided wanting revenge and that blinds them to the damage they are causing to others. They set off chain reactions that cause consequences but the first true exposure to consequences for their actions they see is Ultron and his desire to destroy humanity which makes them instantly want to switch sides. I like Wanda pre-Endgame her arc is from misguided villain to hero despite constantly losing. The path to redemption is paved with alienation and loss. It's beautifully tragic. That said, the point of AoU is that every other step in the process of the missile reaching them is ignored so that they can join Hydra (Nazi's), due to a desire for power they feel they lost, to kill their way to Tony Stark. As covered by Rocket's remarks, their loss shouldn’t be an excuse to get others killed. They are supposed to be scared children, radicalised and misled who eventually realise the extent of what they've created and trying to rectify that mistake. Wanda expands on Tony's trauma by altering his brain to give him a vision that reignites past trauma from Avengers/Iron Man 3, resulting in the creation of Ultron. AoU is about Wanda's redemption including killing the version of Tony Stark she created, Ultron, who represents everything they believed Tony Stark to be; arrogant, narcissistic, manipulator with zero regard for human life who is using his robots to enslave. Tony snapping at Bucky is viewed as a bad thing he does, an emotional outburst, that nearly gets him and others killed and splits the Avengers. Pietro's characterisation is one of the misguided kid who is worried for himself and his sister ultimately paying the ultimate price proving that he was just led astray by his trauma and could have easily been a great hero. Wanda was responsible in the creation of Ultron, so Pietro's death is also her punishment for her decisions as she is more directly involved in weakening the Avengers throughout the movie and as such is more crucial to the defeat of the primary Ultron and his plan at the end of the movie. It's no coincidence that Ultron is primarily born from the trauma of both Wanda and Tony. Howard Stark was the one who created Stark Industries, do we need to consider that? Tony Stark's life was influenced by his parents being killed by the Winter Soldier, do we need to consider that? Bucky only became the Winter Soldier because of Steve saving him from a prison camp and going on a mission with him, do we need to consider that? Steve only became a Super Soldier because of a US program born from fear of Hydra, do we need to consider that? Hydra only gathered powered thanks to the Cosmic Cube/Infinity Stone, do we need to consider that? The Cosmic Cube was retrieved by Red Skull, do we need to consider that? You can go down this sort of blame game forever. At every step characters had a choice and the movie and prequel comic acknowledges it was Wanda & Pietro's decision to go after personal revenge by joining Hydra. Personally I think Clint sacrificing himself because of him wanting to save his family and to give Natasha to get a chance at a normal life, allowing her to accept retiring to be the aunt for his family would have hit harder. That's the fault of Infinity War/Endgame being horrifically written, made by people who disliked well written female characters, like Gamora and Natasha, who had become fan favourites. The writers were embarrassed that the development of Gamora and Natasha put to shame their own handling of female characters such as how Natasha, Sharon Carter and other female characters where handled in Winter Soldier and Civil War - go back and watch those now and you'll see. You can even look toward how Sue Storm is apparently being handled as a prize, an object

posts.text: I think it's an awkward game trying to discuss the morality of fictional characters from the angle being done here. It doesn't really matter the tragic reasons why a character does something is the writers aren't interested in it themselves. Wanda joining a neo nazi group never really comes up past the movie it happens in. This clearly is not something anyone involved cares about, but the same goes for so many other characters. These characters don't actually make decisions of course but I do think looking at these do form some interesting patterns about how this IP is written. I've always thought the MCU doesn't really do redemption, it does the superhero equivalent of category fraud. A character is evil until they are unveiled to be a marketable Superhero then any issues with them are swiftly brushed aside and looked over because they are on the goodie team now. I've discussed this about Jean, the second she is unveiled as Jean Grey the Mutant she is no longer written as moustache twirling and everyone, even Punisher by the end of the film is happy she got away. John Walker is supposed to be super duper evil in the Captain America show until in the finale they want to set up him on the Thunderbolts so he's now just a chill guy doing his best. The exact same thing happens with President Ross who is stock evil military man for over a decade then when he becomes anti-hero red hulk he's a complicated man with a strong heart. No-one really changes they're just put in the good category so we can ignore their past behaviour now. This can happen in reverse too. Jeremy Renner (of Rennervations fame) is a goodie and it's fine when he worked with the nazi inflicted secret agency for years to kill vaguely evil people overseas, but they want him to have a fall from grace so in Endgame he does the same and it's bad now. Him killing Cartel and Yakuza guys is no different in morality or brutality to when Iron-Man kills all those Middle Eastern terrorists in the first Iron-Man but Jeremy Renner is not in the hero category right now so killing stock ethnic movie villains is bad here. Only two have really done a "redemption" by my count (keep in mind this pretty much only takes onto consideration the three bigger TV shows in Wandavision, Captain America and Loki, stuff might have happened in the others) and it's Iron-Man and Loki. But both are also a bit choppy. Iron-Man's issues do come up still in later appearances to be fair, but the issue is from the start that American's were hurt by them. You look at other adaptations like Earth's mightiest heroes and the problem is framed as him having made them at all. While he feels terrible for the troops killed by the Ten Rings with his tech the same thing used to justify Wanda being evil never is really shown to weigh on him. The film doesn't really care that his weapons were used to kill this innocent family, that's just convenient justification to have the twins work with Ultron. So there's a disconnect even in that redemption arc. Then with Loki he does just get a full redemption arc to be fair but then he dies. Then in the Loki show l, despite being Loki before he's grown at all he gets shown a slideshow of the other Loki who was in the hero category and pretty much instantly slots into that role. As soon as the role Loki becomes associated with heroism in the MCU the next one does the category thing and just is good shortly after

posts.title: [MOC] V-19E Super Torrent - Alternate Build of 75432 V-19 Torrent Starfighter
posts.text: What if the Republic had upgraded the V-19 Torrent into a hyperdrive equipped fighter designed to protect ARC-170 formations and give Jedi pilots greater independence? The V-19E Super Torrent retains the original fighter's wide central fuselage, but replaces its complicated folding wings with a fixed delta wing configuration. I wanted to give it a more streamlined, modern fighter profile, taking inspiration from the F-22 Raptor and the classic Buck Rogers starfighter. The raised, canted stabilisers add to the aggressive silhouette, while their position above the wings leaves room for the landing gear underneath. The integrated hyperdrive sits behind the cockpit, allowing the Super Torrent to travel through hyperspace independently without a carrier or separate hyperspace ring. I also moved the laser cannons forward to the front of the engine nacelles, along the wing roots. Placing them closer to the centreline gives the fighter a more naturally aligned forward firing arrangement. During the Clone Wars, the ARC-170 served as a long range heavy fighter for reconnaissance and combat missions. With three clone troopers aboard each aircraft, every loss meant not only the destruction of a valuable fighter, but also the loss of three trained crew members. A dedicated escort like the Super Torrent could have helped protect these valuable ships from enemy starfighters. Its integrated hyperdrive would also have made it useful for Jedi generals, allowing them to travel between systems without relying on the separate hyperspace rings used by many Republic Jedi starfighters. So why didn't the Republic build it? Perhaps the Republic leadership preferred mass producing smaller V-wing interceptors rather than investing in a dedicated escort fighter. The Super Torrent never entered widespread service, becoming one of those intriguing possibilities in an alternative history of the Clone Wars. Like the original donor set, the V-19E Super Torrent is solid and sturdy, making it suitable for both display and play. You can grab it and swoosh it through dogfights across the galaxy without worrying about it falling apart. This is an alternate build of the LEGO Star Wars V-19 Torrent Starfighter set. I hope you enjoy building it as much as I enjoyed designing it! Instructions are on Rebrickable and OpenStuds: https://reb.li/m/278197
